extracted.intended_audience: aspiring periodical-essayists and general authors/essay readers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and implicit evaluation criteria for composing and submitting short, periodical essays — covering craft (diction, composition, structure), presentation (brevity, anonymity), and expectations about publication and reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition requires slow diligence and steady perseverance
rubrics_metrics.description: Composition is, for the most part, an effort of slow diligence and steady perseverance, to which the mind is dragged by necessity or resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writing often lacks the blissful rapid flow of invention; many designs that seem easy in prospect mock us in execution. Expect the mind to be distracted and to require patient, sustained labor rather than instantaneous inspiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Careful choice of words (diction matters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Words, therefore, as well as things, claim the care of an author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good sentiment can be degraded by unsuitable diction; authors frequently struggle to find terms adequate to their conceptions and may need to 'ransack memory' for proper expression. Attention to single epithets or correspondent terms can make or break a period or paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expression is a distinct skill from knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: If words were naturally and necessarily consequential to sentiments...we find, that to think, and discourse, are often the qualities of different persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being well-informed or having noble sentiments doesn't guarantee eloquence; practice and craft are required to render thoughts clearly and elegantly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize and connect thoughts into methodical sequence
rubrics_metrics.description: Sometimes many thoughts present themselves; but so confused and unconnected, that they are not without difficulty reduced to method, or concatenated in a regular and dependent series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid the 'labyrinth' of unconnected ideas. Work to reduce abundance to order — select, arrange, and link ideas into a coherent progression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not overvalue your own judgment; public confirmation is the test
rubrics_metrics.description: From the publick, and only from the publick, is he to await a confirmation of his claim, and a final justification of self-esteem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are partial to their own work; novelty often seduces the producer while failing to convince readers. Reserve final evaluation for the audience rather than self-appraisal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expect public taste to be shaped by a few (influencers/critics)
rubrics_metrics.description: A few, a very few, commonly constitute the taste of the time; the judgment which they have once pronounced, some are too lazy to discuss, and some too timorous to contradict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Realize that exposure to and endorsement by influential readers/critics matters; success often depends less on intrinsic merit than on who praises or propagates the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brevity in submissions — avoid prolixity
rubrics_metrics.description: His letters must not be long; no words are to be squandered in declarations of esteem, or confessions of inability; conscious dulness has little right to be prolix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For contributions to a periodical, be concise. Excessive length, flattering preambles, or self-deprecating confessions are discouraged; brevity is valued by the editor (the Idler).

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity or secrecy about authorship can be advantageous
rubrics_metrics.description: He that is known to contribute to a periodical work, needs no other caution than not to tell what particular pieces are his own; such secrecy is indeed very difficult; but if it can be maintained, it is scarcely to be imagined at how small an expense he may grow considerable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keeping contributions anonymous can let praises 'scatter in the air' and protect contributors from direct censure while allowing them to gain reputation more cheaply than an identified author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stylistic refinement can give value to familiar sentiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Many make it their study, not so much to strike out new sentiments, as to recommend those which are already known to more favourable notice by fairer decorations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Originality of idea is not the only route to merit — careful expression and tasteful presentation of known ideas can win notice. Focus on polishing diction and ornament when invention is limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: To produce novelty in an exhausted field, pursue minute industry and subtle distinctions
rubrics_metrics.description: There is danger lest it be new without novelty... They that follow are forced to peep into neglected corners, to note the casual varieties of the same species, and to recommend themselves by minute industry and distinctions too subtle for common eyes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When major themes are exhausted, novelty arises from close observation, small distinctions, and refined detail rather than grand innovations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion and placement among influential readers is necessary for recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: If a new performance happens not to fall into the hands of some who have courage to tell, and authority to propagate their opinion, it often remains long in obscurity, and perishes unknown and unexamined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical considerations — getting work to those with authority to praise or propagate it — are crucial. Exposure can determine whether a piece reaches public notice regardless of merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be cautious about catering to critics; they can corrupt taste
rubrics_metrics.description: He that assumes the character of a critick...imagines that he is hurting none but the author...little does he think how many honest minds he debars from pleasure, by exciting an artificial fastidiousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize critics' influence but avoid writing solely to please them. Critics may teach affectations that distance ordinary readers; consider the wider readership and not only the instructed censor.
